newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasolines jump after Tosco fire.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasolines jump after Tosco fire.

text.p: U.S. West Coast wholesale gasoline prices jumped two cents in early spot trade Wednesday, following a Tuesday night fire at Tosco's 32,000 barrel-per-day hydrocracker in Martinez, Calif., traders said.
The fire, which started with an explosion overnight, was nearly extinguished by early Wednesday, the company said.
Traders said no deals were done early, with players negotiating ranges until the extent of the refinery's damages emerged.
"There's no (deal) activity yet," a trader said, noting Tosco Corp traders remained out of the market.
But one broker said some deals were done on a private and confidential basis.
Bids for CARB gasoline in Los Angeles were talked about 1.50 cents a gallon higher than Tuesday at 79.50 cents while offers rose the same amount to 80.50 cents.
Conventional gasoline in L.A. was assessed 2.50 cents a gallon higher at 76/77 cents.
"Sellers have popped themselves up a couple cents," a broker said, noting that San Francisco grades also rose two cents, with conventional at 74/75 cents and CARB 77/79 cents.
Distillates saw a more gradual increase in assessments, with low sulphur diesel in L.A. discussed about 0.50 cents a gallon firmer at 80/81 cents.
